SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: “Blinding” headache x 3 days, constant, intensity 8/10 (improves to ~5/10 with Ibuprofen), worst over right eye.
  • Onset: Sudden on waking, 3 days ago.  
  • Character: Diffuse, throbbing; sharp/stabbing on sudden standing or head movement (“feels like something is moving inside”).  
  • Associated symptoms: Photophobia, intermittent “shooting lights”/visual disturbance, mild nausea.  
  • No vomiting, no focal weakness/numbness, no altered smell/taste, no fever, no sinus/cold symptoms, not waking her from sleep.  
  • Partial, temporary relief with Ibuprofen 400 mg? (dose/frequency not documented).
- Impact: Unable to concentrate on work from home; missed 1.5 days of work.
- Past medical history: Childhood abdominal pain (self-resolved, no cause found). No chronic illnesses reported.
- Family history: Mother with severe migraines (with vomiting).
- Medications:
  • Combined oral contraceptive pill – brand/dose not documented (started 1 yr ago).  
  • Ibuprofen PRN for headache – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Denies drug allergies.
- Social history: Lives alone. Non-smoker. Alcohol ~3 drinks once weekly. No recreational drug use.

Objective:
- No physical examination performed during remote consult; no vitals available.
- No investigations performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute severe headache with photophobia & visual phenomena  
   - Assessment: Probable migraine (± aura).  
   - Differential: Cluster headache, tension headache, sinusitis (unlikely), intracranial pathology (e.g., space-occupying lesion, venous thrombosis, subarachnoid hemorrhage).  
   - Investigations planned: In-person neurological examination, fundoscopy, blood pressure measurement.  
   - Treatment: Prescribe stronger NSAID (name/dose/route/frequency not documented) ± concurrent Paracetamol; advise taking with food.  
   - Safety-net: If headache worsens, changes character, or becomes unbearable → attend Emergency Department.

2. Contraceptive pill use in setting of possible migraine with aura  
   - Assessment: Combined oral contraceptive may be contraindicated if migraine with aura confirmed.  
   - Investigations planned: Blood pressure check at upcoming visit.  
   - Treatment/Plan: Continue current pill until evaluation; discuss alternative contraception if migraine with aura diagnosed.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements:  
  – No vitals (BP, pulse, temp).  
  – No documented neurologic or fundoscopic findings.  
  – Medication names/doses/frequencies not fully documented.  
  – Headache red-flag review partially incomplete (e.g., trauma, anticoagulation).  
• Internal conflicts: None identified.  
• Transcript quality: Occasional inaudible sections; minor gaps but core clinical data understandable.
